target_customer: Imaging centers, hospital radiology departments and radiology groups
problem: Radiology image storage and sharing ran on expensive on premise PACS systems; MedXT offered cloud RIS and PACS with an HTML5 viewer.
business_model: pay per use SaaS for cloud RIS and PACS

founders.name: Reshma Khilnani
education: MIT, BS and MEng in EECS
founders.background_notes: From the YC page. Press coverage of the Box deal names a second co-founder, Cody Ebberson, but the YC page lists only Khilnani, so he is not recorded as a founder here.

technical_complexity.rationale: DICOM, HL7 and PACS interoperability plus an FDA cleared viewer, built by a two person team on AWS.

defensibility.rationale: Medical image archives and integrations create switching costs once adopted, but a two person company had few customers and Box could absorb the viewer.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Box bought the company in October 2014 as its first Box for Industries healthcare acquisition and planned to fold the DICOM viewer into its core service.

market_need_then: Radiology groups wanted cloud based image access and sharing; Box and AWS both moved into regulated healthcare storage around this time.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage beyond product and acquisition news; MedXT is confusable with other MedX companies in search results.

outcome_analysis: A two person team launched cloud RIS and PACS in 2014 with an FDA cleared HTML5 viewer and was acquired by Box that October, with undisclosed terms, as Box started its vertical industries push into healthcare. The deal looks like a technology and talent acquisition: the viewer was to be built into Box, and the founders joined Box engineering.
notes: Funding: aggregators only (a Spanish startup directory shows 120k USD seed and 109k EUR, investors N/A), unverified and not recorded as a round. Company site returned HTTP 503 so the website could not be read. Competition: a MedCity News piece lists LifeImage and other image sharing startups but its date was not confirmed as near the batch, so the list is empty. No source explains the name.
